speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether the Government is considering a redefinition of what constitutes basic needs given its evolving understanding which extends beyond traditional necessities like housing and food; (b) if so, will this redefinition take into consideration the need to foster a sense of belonging and living dignity in Singapore; and (c) whether the Government will look into addressing the income inequality gap and relative deprivation, recognising that raising the wage floor may be inadequate to foster this sense of belonging.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) reviews the scheme regularly to ensure that it remains relevant and adequate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: During these reviews, MSF considers the items that should be covered under ComCare, taking into account what other Government schemes or Government-funded programmes would cover, as well as help available through community organisations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Beyond ComCare, other Government schemes and Government-funded programmes enable lower-income individuals to meet other needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Examples include schemes such as MediFund, the Ministry of Education's Financial Assistance Scheme and the Infocomm Media Development Agency's DigitalAccess@Home scheme, which address lower-income families' needs relating to healthcare, education and digital access respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, social service agencies provide befriending services that support seniors' social and psychological well-being and in-kind contributions to assist low-income families with one-off needs, such as furniture and electrical items like refrigerators and washing machines.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Grassroots organisations organise community activities, including affordable local outings and trips to nearby countries, to promote social and family bonding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For lower-income families, grassroots organisations also render support through programmes and initiatives, such as free tuition and local bursary awards for students and monthly free haircuts for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Donors, including corporate donors, have also helped by sponsoring lower-income families for outings to local attractions, such as Universal Studios.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A key feature of ComLink is that Government agencies, social service agencies, corporates and individual volunteers all work together to befriend, encourage and help ComLink families address their needs and challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This collective effort is key to strengthening Singapore's social compact and building a more caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: And as is commonly found by many who volunteer their time and resources to help others, it is not just the recipients of care, concern and resources that gain an increased sense of hope and belonging, those who step forward to give often find that they too have received.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am glad to hear that the Ministry is undertaking this review regularly.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I wish to ask how often will the review take place?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Also, can the Ministry share some details on how the review will be undertaken and will this involve interviewing more residents on the ground?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Specifically, will respondents be surveyed on their personal willingness to pay higher taxes?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And what each respondent will be willing to contribute monthly to support the basic needs of others?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think the question is not one about whether how regular are such reviews but rather whether these supports that we have put in place are adequate and relevant for the families in need.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We also do include items that perhaps over time, should be included in what these families will probably need as a basic need.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I raised the example of mobile data plans as one of the instances that we have included necessities into this basket.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, I hope the Member and other Members of this House are adequately assured that we do review the basket of ComCare support as a basic set of necessities for these families regularly and that the support for these families are adequate and relevant.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Because we are rather slow in our Parliamentary Questions, I am going to move it along.
